etymology: Named in fisheries science: each generation measures the catch against what it remembers, not against what the water held before anyone was counting.
committed_when: A comparison is being made, and the reference point has quietly moved to whatever the speaker grew up with.
tell: The standard of normal is the speaker's own first memory, offered as though it were the original condition.
counter: Ask what the number was before anyone now living was measuring it. A baseline is a record, not a memory.
senses: Judging the present against the last generation's memory instead of the record: the lake still has fish, the river still runs clear enough, the airport still works, so nothing has changed.

It works because every generation is honest and every generation starts late. Nobody alive has seen the earlier state, so the degraded one is the only one anyone can compare against - and the comparison comes out clean every time.
example: *"The lake still has fish in it"* - it has a third of the fish it had when the speaker's father fished it, and the father's father said the same thing about the same lake.

confused_with.tell: Creeping normality is the drift itself, one increment at a time; shifting baseline is why the drift goes unmeasured - each generation resets the ruler.
